title: kv-cache-temporal-decay-and-margined-spill-scheduler
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Introduce a tenant-aware temporal decay policy and a margined spill scheduler to reduce fragmentation-related thrash; improves tail latency and cache utilization for mixed workloads. Rollout via feature flag `kv.temporal_decay_v2` with canary on dedicated clusters.
description:
Motivation: observed recurring thrash on multi-tenant nodes when low-frequency keys are promoted back into hot segments and trigger premature spillovers. This PR introduces a temporal retention-decay model and a margined spill scheduler that cooperates with the scheduler and the kernel hinting path to keep spill bursts bounded.

What this does (high level): implements a decaying retention score (time-decay + access recency) for KV entries, exposes a per-tenant soft-margin which reserves a small buffer of pages to reduce immediate spill pressure, and schedules spill work in a paced fashion (margined spill scheduler) instead of draining aggressively. Adds kernel-level page hinting (MADV_DONTNEED-like signals) for cooled pages to accelerate reclaim without full spill when safe.

Design notes: the temporal score is computed as score = alpha * recency + beta * (1 - e^{-age/tau}) where alpha/beta/tau are tunables exposed in config. The soft-margin is a tenant-level reservation (percentage of cache) that prevents a tenant's low-priority allocations from triggering global spill until global pressure crosses a threshold. The margined spill scheduler groups candidate pages into bounded batches and enforces a backoff window to smooth IO. Interacts with continuous batching: the batcher now tags requests with 'cache-affinity' hints so eviction can avoid hot prefixes currently being actively batched.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for score computation, [x] integration tests for margin behavior, [x] end-to-end perf job, [x] feature-flag gating, [x] docs update stub.

Commits summary: single-feature branch squashed into logical commits: initial temporal-decay model, margin reservation plumbing, margined spill scheduler, kernel hinting integration, tests and perf tuning.

Files touched (high-level): kv/cache/retention.h, kv/cache/retention.cc, kv/scheduler/spill_scheduler.cc, kv/scheduler/spill_scheduler.h, infra/config/kv_flags.yaml, runtimes/linux/page_hints.cc, tests/kv/temporal_decay_test.cc

Testing and perf: locally ran mixed workload A (80% small requests, 20% cold scans) against staging fleet: cache hit rate improved +3.7% and sustained throughput +4.2% at same provision; p99 token latency reduced by 6.1% under spike conditions. Extended soak for 72h on dedicated canaries with feature flag enabled — no regressions observed in memory usage patterns.

Rollout plan: gate under kv.temporal_decay_v2 (default off for existing clusters). Start with 5% of dedicated clusters, monitor hit-rate, p99, and spill IO. If stable after 48h, increase to 25% then full rollout. Fallback: feature flag off and scheduler reverts to legacy immediate-spill path.

Related: follows up on ENG-1142 (tenant-aware quota work) and complements recent spill pacing experiments in ENG-1298.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps migration conservative — we do not change on-disk formats or persisted metadata. The kernel hinting path on some older kernels is a no-op; code guards are in place.
